=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents against the buyer's interests. For EACH of these issues, state the Seller's position, what the buyer should want, and your recommendation with a one-line reason:

# Project Kestrel: Seller Position Review (Buyer Side)

**Overall:** The Seller's package is not a fair or balanced starting point. It is weighted toward the Seller on the caps, thresholds, time limits, knowledge bar, and disclosure. Several known issues (Riverlark debt, Bluefen consent, the export incident, unpaid Ironquay fees, and the bonuses) are either left open or pushed to the Buyer. The "market standard," "settled at principal level," and "FINAL" labels do not bind Wattlebridge. Those positions should be negotiated on their merits, and the deal team should not accept them because they are described as settled.

**Priority items:** SPA-N-008, 009, 010, and 012 should be resolved before signing or completion, and the Buyer should not accept them as post-completion items.

**Summary**

| ID | Issue | Recommendation |
|---|---|---|
| N-001 | General liability cap | Counter |
| N-002 | De minimis & basket | Counter |
| N-003 | General claims time limit | Counter |
| N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | Reject |
| N-005 | Fraud carve-out | Add (absent from Seller draft) |
| N-006 | Disclosure scope | Reject |
| N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | Reject |
| N-008 | Bluefen consent | Reject as drafted |
| N-009 | Riverlark facility | Reject as drafted |
| N-010 | Employee bonuses | Reject as drafted |
| N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | Reject |
| N-012 | Export/privacy incident | Reject; specific indemnity required |
| N-013 | Sandbar renewals | Clarify, then counter |
| N-014 | Category separation | Reject |
| N-015 | Title verification | Accept with conditions |
| N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | Reject |

---

### SPA-N-001: General liability cap

- **Seller:** Aggregate liability for general warranty claims capped at 20% of price (AUD 4.8M).
- **Buyer wants:** A higher general cap (30–40%, roughly AUD 7.2M–9.6M) given the number of known issues and the size of the data-room exposures. Known matters should sit outside the general cap under specific indemnities.
- **Recommendation:** **Counter** at 30%. Accept 20% only if specific indemnities for N-008 to N-012 and the fundamental and tax regimes sit outside it.
- **Reason:** A 20% general cap is tolerable only if known exposures are not forced into it.

### SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket

- **Seller:** De minimis AUD 25,000 (about 0.1% of price). Basket AUD 250,000 (about 1.04%) as a deductible: only the excess is recoverable.
- **Buyer wants:** De minimis around AUD 10,000. A **tipping basket** (once exceeded, recovery from the first dollar) of about 0.5% (AUD 120,000).
- **Recommendation:** **Counter**.
- **Reason:** A deductible basket at the top of the range shifts the first AUD 250,000 of any loss to the Buyer.

### SPA-N-003: General claims time limit

- **Seller:** 18 months from Completion for all claims, with the same period applying to every category.
- **Buyer wants:** 24 months for general warranties. Longer periods for fundamental and tax claims (see N-004 and N-016). Claims in respect of the known issues should run until resolved.
- **Recommendation:** **Counter**.
- **Reason:** 18 months may expire before Bluefen, Riverlark, privacy, or tax exposures crystallise.

### SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime

- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties are subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties.
- **Buyer wants:** Fundamental warranties (title to shares, capacity, authority, share capital) capped at 100% of price, with claims available for at least six years (aligned with the NSW contractual limitation period), and outside the basket and de minimis.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject**.
- **Reason:** The Buyer cannot have a 20% cap or 18-month limit on warranties of its own title.

### SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out

- **Seller:** Clauses 9.3, 12.8, and 20.5 apply exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions to "all Claims of any nature." The Seller draft contains **no fraud carve-out**.
- **Buyer wants:** An express carve-out so that nothing limits liability for fraud, dishonesty, or wilful concealment, including the caps, time limits, exclusive remedy, and non-reliance.
- **Recommendation:** **Add** (required).
- **Reason:** As drafted, the exclusive-remedy and non-reliance language could be read to cover the Seller's own fraud. Do not rely on general law to fill the gap; draft the carve-out expressly.

### SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope

- **Seller:** Clause 1.1 discloses everything in the data room as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, and clause 1.2 discloses the Accounts, statutory registers, and public records.
- **Buyer wants:** Specific disclosure only, with the disclosure against a particular warranty fairly stated. No general data-room or public-register disclosure. Documents referred to in disclosure should be identified individually.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject**.
- **Reason:** General data-room disclosure would strip most warranty protection. The Buyer cannot warrant what it is deemed to have seen.

### SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier

- **Seller:** Clause 8.3 bars claims for any matter the Buyer or its advisers knew of, including anything "discoverable" from the data room or public records.
- **Buyer wants:** Delete clause 8.3. Failing that, limit it to **actual** knowledge of a named individual, exclude constructive or discoverable knowledge, and add an express pro-sandbagging clause, so that the Buyer's diligence does not reduce its claims. The known issues should be dealt with by specific indemnities rather than by knowledge exclusion.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject**.
- **Reason:** Constructive knowledge from the data room would bar claims on the exact issues the Buyer is paying to have covered. Australian law on sandbagging is not settled, so an express clause is needed.

### SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent

- **Seller:** The Seller will use reasonable endeavours. Consent is treated as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent. Disclosure confirms no final written consent or evidence that the clause 11.3 conditions have been met.
- **Buyer wants:** Bluefen consent, in a form satisfying clause 11.2 and all clause 11.3 conditions, as a **condition precedent** to Completion. Failing that, a specific indemnity and price adjustment or holdback tied to the roughly AUD 3.6M revenue (about 30%) at risk.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject as drafted**.
- **Reason:** Bluefen is about 30% of revenue, and "reasonable endeavours" with a loose trigger leaves the Buyer with the loss if consent is refused.

### SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility

- **Seller:** The approximately AUD 3.2M facility will be addressed by a release **after** Completion. Disclosure confirms it is unpaid and there is no final discharge.
- **Buyer wants:** Payoff at Completion, with a payoff letter and release of all security (including any security over shares or assets), funded from the price on a debt-free basis. Change-of-control default waiver if payment is not made.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject as drafted**.
- **Reason:** A post-Completion release leaves the Buyer exposed to lender enforcement over assets it has just bought, and the debt should be settled from the price.

### SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses

- **Seller:** Bonuses of AUD 420,000 are "a matter for the Seller" and are not in the funds flow. Disclosure does not say whether payroll tax, superannuation, or on-costs apply.
- **Buyer wants:** Bonuses (and all related on-costs, including payroll tax and superannuation) treated as **debt-like items** and deducted from price, or paid by the Seller before or at Completion. Note the superannuation guarantee alone (12%) would add about AUD 50,400 on top of AUD 420,000, so the total is about AUD 470,000 before payroll tax.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject as drafted**.
- **Reason:** A debt-like cost left out of the funds flow transfers its full value to the Buyer.

### SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity

- **Seller:** The indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment (AUD 180,000 open per DD-010) and is "considered adequate."
- **Buyer wants:** Payment of all SOW3 fees by the Seller before Completion, with a confirmatory assignment of Project Materials (clause 7.3 condition satisfied). A specific indemnity, outside the cap and basket, for third-party IP claims, title defects, and costs to remediate the Project Materials. Evidence of payment or no-dispute confirmation.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject**.
- **Reason:** The Buyer is exposed to IP title and third-party claims that the AUD 180,000 figure does not capture.

### SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident

- **Seller:** The DD-006 incident is "preliminary" and "not expected to be material." It may involve about 1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). The scope, access, and notification status are not established. No loss amount is given.
- **Buyer wants:** Before Completion, a completed forensic review and a documented assessment under the Notifiable Data Breaches scheme in the *Privacy Act 1988* (Cth). Confirm whether the company is an APP entity and whether an eligible data breach has occurred, and assess whether the 30-day assessment window has already run. Also a specific privacy warranty and an uncapped (or 100%-capped) indemnity outside the basket, backed by a retention or escrow.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject; specific indemnity required**.
- **Reason:** The incident may trigger statutory notification and regulatory and individual exposure, and the Seller has not quantified it. The 22 September data-room cut-off also means the current status needs to be confirmed.

### SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals

- **Seller:** Three renewals (AUD 110,000 each, AUD 330,000 aggregate) are "ordinary-course operating costs."
- **Buyer wants:** Confirmation of term, termination rights, prepayment or commitment status, and whether any renewal extends beyond Completion. Any prepaid, multi-year, or non-terminable element should be treated as a seller cost or working-capital adjustment. Renewals of operating contracts should be covered by the ordinary-course warranty.
- **Recommendation:** **Clarify, then counter**.
- **Reason:** The disclosure does not say whether the costs are accrued, prepaid, or terminable, and that determines whether they are an operating cost or a debt-like item.

### SPA-N-014: Category separation

- **Seller:** Uniform regime for all warranty claims.
- **Buyer wants:** Separate regimes for (a) fundamental, (b) tax, (c) privacy, and (d) known matters, each with its own cap, time limit, and carve-outs from the basket and de minimis. General warranties on the existing 20–30% cap and 24-month limit.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject**.
- **Reason:** Uniform limits treat title, tax, and known issues the same as ordinary commercial warranties, which understates their risk.

### SPA-N-015: Title verification

- **Seller:** Title is "evidenced by" the share register at DD-012, showing Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100%. The Seller notes this does not mean the Buyer has verified title.
- **Buyer wants:** Independent verification: an ASIC company extract and current-register check, inspection of the register of members, a PPSR search over the shares, and confirmation that no encumbrances exist. A stock transfer form in agreed form and a title warranty from the Seller (see N-004).
- **Recommendation:** **Accept with conditions**.
- **Reason:** The register is the Seller's evidence, and the Buyer's own searches must be completed before relying on it.

### SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms

- **Seller:** Tax and IP warranties are "settled under the general regime."
- **Buyer wants:** A pre-Completion tax indemnity (capped at 100% of price) for pre-Completion taxes, with a limitation period running at least until the ATO's amendment window for the relevant years has closed. Specific IP warranties on ownership, non-infringement, and open-source use, with the IP-specific carve-outs from N-011 applied.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject**.
- **Reason:** Tax exposure and IP title typically crystallise after the general 18–24 month window.

---

### Other items outside the 16 IDs

- **Office lease (DD-007):** Confirm whether landlord consent is required for the share sale, not only notice. If so, make it a condition precedent.
- **Mossvale (DD-009):** Confirm whether the assignment restriction is triggered by a share sale. If so, obtain consent or a waiver.

### Caveats

This is a buyer-side analysis based only on the Seller's documents and disclosure letter. Statutory references (the *Privacy Act 1988* (Cth) NDB scheme, the NSW limitation period, and ATO amendment periods) should be confirmed by NSW counsel and tax advisers before the positions go into the mark-up. The percentages proposed are opening positions for negotiation, not market quotes.

- **Buyer wants:** Separate regimes for (a) fundamental, (b) tax, (c) privacy, and (d) known matters, each with its own cap, time limit, and carve-outs from the basket and de minimis. General warranties on the existing 20–30% cap and 24-month limit.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject**.
- **Reason:** Uniform limits treat title, tax, and known issues the same as ordinary commercial warranties, which understates their risk.

### SPA-N-015: Title verification

- **Seller:** Title is "evidenced by" the share register at DD-012, showing Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100%. The Seller notes this does not mean the Buyer has verified title.
- **Buyer wants:** Independent verification: an ASIC company extract and current-register check, inspection of the register of members, a PPSR search over the shares, and confirmation that no encumbrances exist. A stock transfer form in agreed form and a title warranty from the Seller (see N-004).
- **Recommendation:** **Accept with conditions**.
- **Reason:** The register is the Seller's evidence, and the Buyer's own searches must be completed before relying on it.

### SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms

- **Seller:** Tax and IP warranties are "settled under the general regime."
- **Buyer wants:** A pre-Completion tax indemnity (capped at 100% of price) for pre-Completion taxes, with a limitation period running at least until the ATO's amendment window for the relevant years has closed. Specific IP warranties on ownership, non-infringement, and open-source use, with the IP-specific carve-outs from N-011 applied.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject**.
- **Reason:** Tax exposure and IP title typically crystallise after the general 18–24 month window.
